findings.title: [P3] Repeated reads of `current` IDs change observable evaluation behavior
findings.body: The old code read each `current[*].id` exactly once (eager `Set` construction); the new code reads all of them once per `previous` element, and skips reading them entirely when `previous` is empty. For plain data this is unobservable, but for getter/proxy-backed `id` accessors that mutate or throw, evaluation counts, ordering, and results can differ (e.g. a getter returning `"a"` then `"b"` with `previous` IDs `["a","b"]` yields `[]` instead of `["b"]`). Low impact given no in-repo callers or type constraints on `Item`; fixing the P2 by snapshotting IDs once also eliminates this.
